title: Drop-seq: original 2015 general single-cell droplet RNA capture assay
scope: General original Macosko et al. 2015 Drop-seq assay: preparation of required barcoded beads and co-flow device, intact single-cell suspension interface, cell/bead droplet partitioning and lysis/poly(A) RNA capture, bead recovery, bulk reverse transcription/template switching, unextended-primer removal, cDNA amplification, 3-prime sequencing-library formation and paired readout/decoding to cell-associated gene molecule counts. Retain original bead/primer variants and source-reported choices/unknowns. Exclude exact historical retina/cohort recreation, cell culture/animal details as universal requirements, clustering and biological discovery, later assay variants, and unqualified transfer of optimized online-protocol recipes. Original full paper and original supplementary information are authoritative; binary originals and figure layouts remain available beside registered text renditions. The registered Illumina manufacturer source is Part 15031942 Rev.D (September 2014), selected faithful scan transcriptions for the delegated Nextera XT mechanism/tagmentation/neutralization and cleanup context. The exact historical guide revision is not stated by the paper. Applicability must be justified; general guide input, PCR, indexing, elution, normalization and instrument defaults do not override the original paper/supplement modifications.

operations.name: Fragment cDNA and add Nextera adapters
operations.action: Tagment each original 600-pg cDNA aliquot using standard Nextera XT as delegated by the supplement. The contemporaneous Rev.D guide explains simultaneous fragmentation/adapter-end addition and gives TD 10 uL, ATM 5 uL, heated-lid 55 C 5 min then 10 C hold. These are explicitly manufacturer-context conditions for the delegated operation, not proof of the historical guide revision. Its 5-uL, 1-ng DNA default does not replace the paper's 600-pg mass; actual original DNA volume remains unknown.

unresolved.description: Supplemental implementation notes call 50 cells/uL a standard final concentration, and separately specify bead feed 120/uL giving 60/uL in droplets. Figure S3 caption explicitly describes a 50-cells/uL concentration in droplets for its impurity experiment; the culture dilution and retina preparation paragraphs describe their suspension concentrations. These have different sample/experiment anchors, so the record neither declares them contradictory nor silently assigns every reported cell concentration to the same syringe/droplet reference. This does not block the generic equal-aqueous-flow interface.
unresolved.next_evidence: A source-specific clarification mapping the implementation-note standard 50 cells/uL to pre-co-flow suspension versus final droplet concentration, if an execution concentration is required.

These are nonblocking recipe details for the explicit bead-to-amplified-cDNA boundary, not permission to execute an inferred universal PCR.
